Baby Corn Gratin

Served at: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)

Serves 6-8Prep 20 minCook 30 min

Baby Corn Gratin is a comforting and creamy dish, perfect for a reflective family meal. On the Feast of the Holy Innocents, also known as Childermas, this warm gratin offers a sense of solace and care, honoring the memory of the innocent while providing a nourishing dish suitable for all ages at the banquet table.

Ingredients

  • 2 (15 ounce / 425g) cans baby corn, drained and rinsed
  • 4 tablespoons (56g) unsalted butter
  • 4 tablespoons (30g) all-purpose flour
  • 2 cups (480ml) whole milk, warmed
  • 1.5 cups (170g) shredded Gruyère or sharp cheddar cheese, divided
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
  • Pinch of freshly grated nutmeg
  • 1/2 cup (60g) panko breadcrumbs

Method

  1. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Lightly grease a 9x13 inch (23x33 cm) baking dish.
  2. If using canned baby corn, ensure it is well-drained and patted dry. If using frozen, thaw and pat dry.
  3. In a medium saucepan over medium heat, melt the butter. Add the flour and whisk constantly for 1-2 minutes to create a roux.
  4. Gradually whisk in the warm milk, a little at a time, ensuring no lumps form. Continue whisking until the sauce thickens, about 5-7 minutes.
  5. Remove the saucepan from the heat. Stir in 1 cup (113g) of the shredded cheese, salt, pepper, and nutmeg until the cheese is melted and fully incorporated.
  6. Add the drained baby corn to the cheese sauce and stir gently to coat evenly.
  7. Pour the baby corn mixture into the prepared baking dish, spreading it into an even layer.
  8. In a small bowl, combine the remaining 1/2 cup (57g) shredded cheese with the panko breadcrumbs. Sprinkle this mixture evenly over the top of the gratin.
  9. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the gratin is bubbly around the edges and the topping is golden brown and crisp.
  10. Let the gratin rest for 5-10 minutes before serving to allow it to set slightly.

Tips

  • For an extra layer of flavor, sauté a finely minced shallot or a clove of garlic in the butter before adding the flour for the roux.
  • This gratin can be assembled ahead of time. Cover and refrigerate for up to 24 hours, then bake as directed, adding an extra 5-10 minutes to the cook time if baking from cold.
  • Consider adding a pinch of cayenne pepper or a dash of hot sauce to the cheese sauce for a subtle kick that complements the sweetness of the baby corn.
